newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack output at 65,000 BPD.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack output at 65,000 BPD.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday that production at the Cossack-Pioneer oil rig offshore of Western Australia had managed to ramp up production to at least 65,000 barrels a day after having reduced output to about 40,000 barrels last week.

Meanwhile, a Woodside spokesman told Reuters all non-essential staff on the platform had been evacuated and preliminary measures were underway to disconnect the mooring and halt production if a tropical low off the coast presented a danger. "These preliminary steps have not affected production," the spokesman said.
The Cossack-Pioneer had been placed on "red cyclone alert" for the low, which had the potential to build into a cyclone, the spokesman said.
At 0350 GMT (11.50 a.m. local time), the low was located 600 km north-west of the coastal community of Karratha and heading southeast the Bureau of Meteorology said.
"It could turn into a cyclone in the next 24 hours," a bureau spokesman said.
The rig's offtake housing had been disconnected as part of the procedures for disconnection from the mooring if required, the Woodside spokesman said.
The facility was forced to reduce output to about 40,000 bpd from about 80,000 bpd last week after a faulty steam heating device was encountered.
The spokesman said it was hoped that production could be ramped up further and maintained ahead of the scheduled arrival of a replacement part in mid-March.
"We'd like to get production up and keep it there," he said.
Last October, maintenance work on the gas export system of the Cossack-Pioneer reduced production to about 50,000 bpd for several weeks.
The facility also has had to disconnect from its mooring on several occassions to flee the path of tropical cyclones.

Equal-stake partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer field is situated, are units of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and operator Woodside Petroleum.
